name: Treated-effluent discharge boundary (press: Pyeongtaek public wastewater treatment plant → Seojeongni stream)
note: Press (as of 2020): the Pyeongtaek campus used about 67,000 t of water a day on average, and about 54,000 t was discharged to Seojeongni stream via the Pyeongtaek city wastewater treatment plant. Building register: 'sewage and similar treatment facility' at Godeok-dong 1721 (Samsung 1-ro 60) — site 150,297.2㎡, building area 8,429.26㎡, total floor area 21,840.49㎡, use approval 2022-07-15. The register alone does not establish that this is the Godeok public wastewater treatment plant named in the press. Path (press on a Gyeonggi Province inspection, 2026-10): on-site water treatment 'green building' (primary treatment) → Godeok public wastewater treatment plant → Seojeongni stream → Jinwi stream → Anseong stream → Pyeongtaek lake. The 17 PFAS reported by a civic group in 2026-10 came from a sample taken at the final outlet of the Godeok industrial complex public wastewater treatment plant (Godeok-dong 2745, Seojeongni stream); press reports note that this plant also receives treated water from facilities other than Samsung Electronics, so the whole amount cannot be attributed to Samsung Electronics. Samsung Electronics plan (press): pilot unit for PFAS separation/concentration followed by electrochemical treatment to be installed 2026-12 and applied 2027-08. The effluent temperature-reduction facility uses thermal-energy recovery rather than cooling towers, targeting about 30 ℃ → 17 ℃ or below, with commissioning 2026-12 to 2027-02. The locations of the temperature-reduction facility and the pilot unit are not public and are not modelled. This box is a concept marker, not the coordinates of the actual outlet

name: Air Products Korea Pyeongtaek plant site (map label; read from satellite imagery)
note: Plan measured from satellite imagery; height and use are estimates. Press (2026-05): the Pyeongtaek plant accounts for about 40% of the company's gas output, has about 729.6 kW of rooftop solar for its own use, and is building additional supply facilities in step with the campus expansion. name: Samsung Electronics logistics warehouse — relocation planned (Kakao Map label · read from imagery · presumed CDC logistics centre; press reports a move to the new Poseung CDC)
note: Plan measured from satellite imagery; height and use are estimates. Plan read from satellite imagery (Esri World Imagery, zoom 18, about 0.48 m/px, re-acquired 2026-11-13) with an error of about ±5 m. Cylindrical tanks and process equipment are simplified as boxes. The building Kakao Map labels 'Samsung Electronics logistics warehouse' (logistics centre, Godeok-dong 1696-1). In the 2025-12-22 satellite imagery it is a single-roof building of about 177 × 320 m (about 56,600㎡) with rows of loading docks on its east and west sides. Height estimated at about 21 m from the shadow length (about 37 m). No entry was returned by the public building register. Press (2025-12): the CDC logistics centre on the planned P6 site is to be demolished by May 2026, and the demolition permit has been issued. A CDC (Central Distribution Center) is a central logistics centre that handles receiving, storage, sorting and delivery of products; Samsung Electronics is building a home-appliance CDC of about 110,000㎡ in the Pyeongtaek Poseung district (started 2025-03, completion targeted 2027-06; investment agreement reported 2026-09). Read together, the reports describe a product distribution centre rather than a fab materials warehouse, and a relocation to Poseung rather than a closure. However, no source states directly that this Kakao Map building is the CDC in the press, or that the Poseung centre replaces it, so both are inferences; whether it has been demolished was not confirmed. Further checks (press 2020): the Samsung Electronics Pyeongtaek integrated logistics centre (CDC) was completed in 2018, handles logistics for most Samsung home appliances such as TVs, refrigerators and air conditioners, and is managed by the subsidiary Samsung Electronics Logitech. In 2025-12 another outlet also reported the plan to demolish the CDC on the planned P6 site and that the permit had been obtained. The Poseung centre is expected to distribute appliances made in Korea and products made abroad arriving through Pyeongtaek port (press 2026-09). Press in 2026: the fab after P5 is planned as a twin fab with the same structure as P5 (P5-2), and site workers say excavation has started — this is not direct confirmation that this building has been demolished. A layout graphic made by a YouTube real-estate channel (2026-09, watched muted) draws P5 Fab 2 immediately north of P5 Fab 1, and this warehouse falls in its north-west corner — it is not an official drawing and is used only as a reference. This model therefore labels the building as relocation planned
